prompt:
The maps below show a public park in the town of Ashcombe in 2002 and the same park in 2024.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
instruction_line: You should spend about 20 minutes on this task. Write at least 150 words.

visual.alt: Two maps showing the public park in the town of Ashcombe side by side in 2002 and 2024: the pond and car park have been enlarged, a wooden walkway has been built across the pond, a café has replaced the flower garden, the southern half of the lawn has become a sports pitch, the play area has been extended, a cycle path and a new footbridge have been added along the stream; the road, the stream, the trees and the footpath stay the same.

key_points: Over twenty-two years, the park changes from a quiet green space into an area offering more activities and easier access; its boundaries (Mill Road to the north, the stream to the south) stay the same
Two of the three features in the northern strip change: the car park is nearly doubled in size and a café replaces the flower garden; the play area is kept but extended southwards
The pond in the west is enlarged and a wooden walkway is built across it, allowing people to cross from one side to the other
The biggest area change is in the middle: the southern half of the wide lawn is turned into a sports pitch, while the northern half stays as lawn
There are two new transport features in the south: a cycle path running alongside the stream and a footbridge over the stream, giving the park a second entrance from the south
What stays unchanged: the road to the north, the stream to the south, the row of trees along the eastern edge, and the footpath crossing the park from east to west
common_mistakes: Not using direction and location language ('in the north-west corner', 'along the eastern edge', 'to the south of the lawn')
Describing the two maps separately without highlighting the change — change is the real focus of this task
Never mentioning the features that stay unchanged (the road, the stream, the trees, the footpath)
Mixing up tenses; failing to use the past tense for 2002 and the present tense for 2024
Interpreting or justifying the change ('the council wanted to attract more young families')
